gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions (probe-verified against the real WASM)

gaps.missing: imports kind misclassified usage_contextual instead of import_based — the tier classifier has no 'imports' branch (the TS T1 / JVM K8 finding): every ES6/require/re-export dependency edge falls to usage_contextual
gaps.evidence: probe: import def from './m' -> imports: probe -> ./m:def conf=1 evidenceClass=usage_contextual (expect import_based)

gaps.missing: dynamic import('./lazy') emits a spurious calls -> import edge and NO imports edge for the module — TS7 was closed in the TS wave; the JS dynamic-import fixture currently documents the bug as accepted
gaps.evidence: probe: const lazy = import('./lazy') -> calls: probe -> import (spurious); no imports edge for ./lazy

gaps.missing: string interpolation `${x}` emits no Uses on the interpolated identifiers (TS3 T3 / kotlin K4 / scala G4 analog)
gaps.evidence: probe: const s = `hi ${n} x` inside method -> no uses edge on n

gaps.missing: obj.method() emits BOTH calls (obj.method -> method) AND uses (obj -> method, isFieldAccess) — the family contract (TS/kotlin/scala) skips the callee in uses because calls covers it; JS double-emits
gaps.evidence: probe: obj.method() -> calls: method -> method AND uses: obj -> method

gaps.missing: calls inside static { } blocks attribute to the MODULE, not the enclosing class — kotlin K7 init-attribution analog
gaps.evidence: probe: class A { static { initStatic(); } } -> calls: probe-js1 -> initStatic (expect A)

gaps.missing: top-level const r = x instanceof T attributes the reference to 'global' instead of r — the resolveSource walk lacks variable_declarator (TS fixed this in the same wave)
gaps.evidence: probe: const r = obj instanceof TopLevel -> references: global -> TopLevel (expect r)

gaps.missing: module-level destructured bindings (const { a } = obj / const [b] = arr) emit NO symbols — TS emits them as constants (probe-verified parity gap)
gaps.evidence: probe: const { d2 } = someObj -> no symbol; TS same shape -> a [constant]

gaps.missing: JSX component usage emits NOTHING — <Button/> produces no edges. JSX is native to the JS grammar (8 types in the gate enumeration), unlike TS where it is a separate tsx dialect; the analyzer's detectsJsx only sets a pattern flag
gaps.evidence:
probe: const App = () =>
-> no uses/instantiates edges for Button

decisions.question: typeParameters payload: JavaScript has NO generics — the grammar declares no type_parameters node. Recommend: DECLARED N/A (omit from the payload matrix), consistent with the family contract that payloads exist only where the language declares them.
apiContract payload: JS has no framework API-contract concept (TS's api-contract is typed). Recommend: DECLARED N/A (groovy also omits it).
[key]: value computed names are recursed generically with no dedicated symbol — recommend INTERNAL SILENT (TS D6 consistency).
Glimmer/Ember templates are declared by the grammar but ignored — recommend INTERNAL SILENT (TS D4 consistency).
class static blocks: the block is recursed (calls found) but attribution lands on the module — J5 covers the attribution fix; the block structure itself is handled.
